title: Sieva lima bean (Sieva patani): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Sieva lima bean: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Sieva lima bean is a lima bean variety from UPCA (now UPLB). See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Sieva is a registered lima bean variety, also sold or known as Sieva patani. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1972. UPCA bred it. It takes 60 to 70 days from sowing to harvest.

heroImage.alt: Young mungbean rows beside paddy fields in Candaba, Pampanga, the kind of farm where Sieva lima bean is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Sieva patani, this is the same lima bean. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [lima bean variety finder](/crop-varieties/lima-bean), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for legumes](/land-preparation/legume-land-preparation).

items: **Days to harvest:** 60 to 70 days from sowing to harvest.

blocks.text: Key facts about Sieva lima bean

blocks.caption: From the NSIC registry and its seller

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Sieva lima bean takes 60 to 70 days from sowing to harvest. That is 4 days faster than the average of the 5 lima bean varieties with a day count, 69 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more. Its seller gives 60 to 70 days.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit lima bean fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer), [powdery mildew](/diseases/powdery-mildew). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

Why farmers know it: one of the first two lima beans on the Philippine Seed Board list, current seed sellers not confirmed. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Sieva lima bean

Patani climbs and bears for a long time. Pick a variety by seed size and color, and give it a strong trellis. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items.q: Is Sieva patani the same as Sieva?
items.a: Yes. Sieva patani is another name for Sieva. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 60 to 70 days from sowing to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Sieva?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
